commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Regenerate rewrites 1(h) formulas: adjusted_net_capital_gain_limited floors taxable_income at 0, 28% gain tax is now capped by remaining taxable income, net_capital_gain subtracts the 163(d)(4)(B)(iii) election amount, and many source cites are corrected.
description: the net capital gain for any taxable year shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount which the taxpayer takes into account as investment income under section 163(d)(4)(B)(iii)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module omitted the 26 USC 1(h)(2) reduction of net capital gain by the amount the taxpayer elects to take into account as investment income under section 163(d)(4)(B)(iii), and applied the 28% rate to the entire 28-percent rate gain instead of to 1(h)(1)(F)'s base of taxable income in excess of the amounts already taxed under the preceding subparagraphs, so both net capital gain and the 28% tax came out too high.
triage.triage_notes: Multi-defect fidelity fix in one module; both dominant defects are the same kind (a clause the source states that the encoding did not represent). (1) net_capital_gain: parent formula was max(0, max(0,LTCG) - max(0,-STCG)) + QDI; post adds `- net_capital_gain_taken_into_account_as_investment_income_under_section_163_d_4_B_iii` inside the max(0, ...), matching 1(h)(2)'s 'reduced (but not below zero)'. The identifier is an external input (not declared as a rule in either version; the test file adds it as us:statutes/26/1/h#input....). A renamed test case, `investment_income_reduces_net_capital_gain`, exercises it (5000 election drops net_capital_gain 30000 -> 25000). (2) capital_gains_28_percent_rate_gain_tax: parent was `capital_gains_28_percent_rate * capital_gains_28_percent_rate_gain`; post wraps the base in min(..., max(0, taxable_income - non_capital_gain_taxable_income - zero/15/20 brackets - taxable_unrecaptured_section_1250_gain)), which is 1(h)(1)(F)'s 'amount of taxable income in excess of the sum of the amounts on which tax is determined under the preceding subparagraphs'. The reworked test does not actually bind that cap (0.28*5000=1400 either way). (3) adjusted_net_capital_gain_limited: min(ANCG, taxable_income) -> min(ANCG, max(taxable_income, 0)); a smaller negative-taxable-income floor fix, arguably boundary_direction on its own, but it is secondary to the two missing-clause fixes and I did not make it the reported kind. Provision read: resolve_provision.py on us/statute/26/1 at this rulespec commit succeeded and the corpus text contains both 1(h)(2) and 1(h)(1)(F) verbatim as the new proof excerpts quote them. Caveats: commit message is the bare subject 'Regenerate capital gains rate RuleSpec' with an empty body and there is no PR in the bundle, so the quote is an added proof-atom excerpt line inside the module diff rather than a `#` comment or maintainer prose - hence confidence held below 0.8. The same commit also makes provenance-only edits across most other rules (span -> excerpt proof atoms, narrowed `source:` cites, 1(j)(5) cites moved between rules, block-scalar reflow of constant formulas, imports narrowed from the whole rev-proc-2025-32 module to two named outputs) that do not change meaning; one oddity worth a reviewer's eye is that two different imported outputs (capital_gains_zero_rate_threshold and capital_gains_fifteen_percent_threshold) carry the identical import hash sha256:396e2861..., which looks like a module-level rather than per-output hash.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes encoded meaning, not just provenance: `net_capital_gain`'s formula gains a subtraction term and `capital_gains_28_percent_rate_gain_tax` goes from `capital_gains_28_percent_rate * capital_gains_28_percent_rate_gain` to that rate times `min(capital_gains_28_percent_rate_gain, max(0, taxable_income - non_capital_gain_taxable_income - ... - taxable_unrecaptured_section_1250_gain))`. Both are clauses the pinned corpus text of 26 USC 1 states and the pre-fix module omitted: 1(h)(2) ("For purposes of this subsection, the net capital gain for any taxable year shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount which the taxpayer takes into account as investment income under section 163(d)(4)(B)(iii)") and 1(h)(1)(F)'s base ("28 percent of the amount of taxable income in excess of the sum of the amounts on which tax is determined under the preceding subparagraphs of this paragraph"), both verified verbatim in release us-rulespec-2026-07-13. The companion test file corroborates the behavior change rather than a rename: a new case `investment_income_reduces_net_capital_gain` feeds a 5000 election and drops `net_capital_gain` from 30000 to 25000, and the 28% case's tax falls from 2800 to 1400 under the new cap. The one refutation I could mount — that the pre-fix rule only claimed 1(h)(11)/1222(11) scope, so 1(h)(2) is new coverage — fails because this module is scoped to subsection (h) and the rule feeds 1(h)(1)(A) and 1(h)(1)(E) formulas, where 1(h)(2)'s "for purposes of this subsection" reduction is mandatory.
triage.verifier_notes: Kind held at unrepresented_clause after considering two alternatives. (1) untraceable_branch for the 28% rule: the pre-fix rule was cited to "26 USC 1(h)(1)(F), 1(h)(4)" and taxed the 28-percent rate gain directly, which is (h)(4)'s defined term rather than (F)'s statutory base, so "grounded on the wrong provision" is arguable — but the fix keeps the gain term and wraps it in a min() cap, i.e. it adds the missing limitation rather than removing or re-grounding a baseless branch, so unrepresented_clause fits better and covers both formula changes under one kind. (2) not_a_defect as scope expansion: rejected for the reason in the justification; note that the fix does introduce a brand-new external input (`input.net_capital_gain_taken_into_account_as_investment_income_under_section_163_d_4_B_iii`, added to every test case), so a reviewer who treats a new required input as new scope rather than as the encoding mechanism for an existing clause could land on unclear. A third change, `adjusted_net_capital_gain_limited` going from `min(adjusted_net_capital_gain, taxable_income)` to `min(adjusted_net_capital_gain, max(taxable_income, 0))`, is a defensive floor with no explicit source phrase requiring it; on its own that element would be not_a_defect/unclear and it is not load-bearing here. The remaining ~80% of the 414-line diff is mechanical: `span:` keys replaced by `excerpt:` strings, module summary replaced with corpus text, block-scalar reflow of unchanged scalars (e.g. `'0.20'` to a literal block), and source-cite string edits such as dropping ", 1(j)(5)" from the 20% rate. Commit body is empty ("\n") and the subject is the generic "Regenerate capital gains rate RuleSpec", so no commit-message evidence exists; the verdict rests entirely on the diff, the test deltas, and the resolved corpus text (provision file sha256 1b0b185ca3335eb06c4fe10af488a8984bdd2cedd4087badf78583c267af7b7b). The same commit also touches statutes/26/199A.yaml (13 lines), which imports this `net_capital_gain` rule; that module was not assessed here.
